interactions.summary: Jiang argues that students rarely get enough autonomy to learn accurate self-assessment, then proposes the learning journal as a coronavirus-era structure for self-directed meta-learning with teachers acting as coaches.

claims.claim: Jiang says the hardest thing for students to learn is accurate self-assessment.
He argues that schools usually do not give children enough space or autonomy to develop self-reflection and self-assessment.
Jiang treats the coronavirus disruption as a moment when students have more time to suffer, self-reflect, and self-assess, so schools should actively promote meta-learning.
The learning journal model lets students choose their own learning path, regardless of whether the project is cooking, driving, programming, or another concrete challenge.
A learning journal has three parts: define the goal concretely, record the learning process, and write observations and data that support self-reflection and new strategy formation.
Teachers remain essential in this model, but their role shifts from giving answers to coaching students.
Jiang defines coaching through three functions: motivate the student, inspect the journal for weaknesses or trouble spots, and suggest new learning strategies.
The coach should not hand over correct solutions but should widen the student's field of options so the student can diagnose their own learning more accurately.
Jiang predicts that students who use a learning journal during the disruption will return to the classroom more motivated and more effective as learners.
claims.temporal_scope: Forward-looking educational prediction from 2020-07-22 about post-pandemic classroom return.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns pandemic disruption into a training ground for self-assessment by saying students now have time to suffer, self-reflect, and self-assess.
signature_moments.source_phrase: kids have all this time to suffer self-reflect and self-assess
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the clip its edge: crisis is not just lost schooling but an opening for meta-learning that normal school routines suppress.

signature_moments.moment: He reduces the learning journal to a three-part method: precise goal, documented process, and observed data that generate better strategies.
signature_moments.source_phrase: three components to a learning journal
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the operational core of the clip and makes the idea reusable rather than inspirational fluff.

signature_moments.moment: The coach's job is not to supply the right answer but to open new possibilities so the student can diagnose the learning problem for themselves.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the idea is not to give correct solutions
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It sharply redefines teaching as option-generation and metacognitive calibration rather than answer delivery.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's structured record of self-directed learning in which a student chooses a goal, documents the process, and reflects on observations to improve strategy.
Learning about how one learns, especially through self-reflection and self-assessment during an unstructured period.
Jiang's phrase for the hard educational skill of judging one's own performance and learning state truthfully enough to improve it.
The teacher role in the learning-journal model: motivate, identify weak spots, and suggest strategies rather than deliver the right answer.

chronology_notes.note: This source is explicitly anchored to the first-wave coronavirus schooling disruption in mid-2020 and ties the learning-journal proposal to time away from the physical classroom.

uncertainty_notes.note: ASR renders the second coaching function as 'identify witnesses in the learning journal'; context suggests Jiang likely means weaknesses, glitches, or trouble spots rather than literal witnesses.
The phrase 'finish challenge' is likely a mistranscription of a named challenge or benchmark and should not be treated as a stable term.
